title: Jak dojdę do Rynku?
titleEn: How do I get to the Main Square?
focus: motion verbs: iść and chodzić, jechać, and prefixes

patterns.determinate: Iść vs. chodzić: one direction now vs. around or habitually
patterns.prefix: Motion prefixes: do- (reach), prze- (across), po- (set off), w- (into)
patterns.aspect: Aspect pair: zgubić się / gubić się
patterns.formal: Formal you: pan / pani + 3rd person verb
patterns.speaker: Gender follows the speaker

lines.speaker: Ania
lines.pl: Przepraszam, zgubiłam|zgubilam się. Jak dojdę|dojde do Rynku|rynku?
lines.en: Excuse me, I’m lost. How do I get to the Main Square?

lines.speaker: Przechodzień
lines.pl: Idzie|idzie pani w złą|zla stronę|strone. Proszę zawrócić|zawrocic i przejść|przejsc przez ulicę|ulice na światłach|swiatlach.
lines.en: You’re going the wrong way. Turn back and cross the street at the lights.

lines.speaker: Ania
lines.pl: A potem? Czy to daleko? Może lepiej pojadę|pojade tramwajem|tramwajem?
lines.en: And then? Is it far? Maybe I’d better take the tram?

lines.speaker: Przechodzień
lines.pl: Nie warto|warto, to piętnaście minut pieszo|pieszo. Najpierw dojdzie|dojdzie pani do Wawelu|wawelu, potem skręci|skreci pani w Grodzką|grodzka i pójdzie|pojdzie pani prosto aż do Rynku.
lines.en: It’s not worth it, it’s fifteen minutes on foot. First you’ll get to Wawel, then you turn into Grodzka Street and go straight on all the way to the square.

lines.speaker: Ania
lines.pl: Dziękuję! Codziennie chodzę|chodze po mieście|miescie z mapą|mapa w telefonie|telefonie, a i tak się gubię|gubie.
lines.en: Thank you! I walk around the city every day with a map on my phone, and I still get lost.

lines.speaker: Przechodzień
lines.pl: Każdy się tu gubi. Ja mieszkam|mieszkam w Krakowie|krakowie od dwudziestu|dwudziestu lat|lat, a wczoraj wjechałem|wjechalem w ślepą|slepa uliczkę|uliczke!
lines.en: Everyone gets lost here. I’ve lived in Kraków for twenty years, and yesterday I drove into a dead end!

lines.speaker: Ania
lines.pl: No to mnie pan pocieszył|pocieszyl! Do widzenia!

zgubilam.tags: verb · perfective · past · 1st person singular · feminine
zgubilam.why: Perfective: the getting lost has happened, and she is now lost. Its imperfective partner, gubić się, describes getting lost again and again (line 5).

you.f: You would say: zgubiłam się, as Ania does.

dojde.tags: verb · perfective · non-past (future meaning) · 1st person singular
parts: root of iść (id-); i → j after a prefix
dojde.why: Do- adds “all the way to”: dojść do Rynku, “to get as far as the square.” It goes with do + genitive. Being perfective, the present-tense form refers to the future: “how will I get there?”
dojde.compare: By vehicle: Jak dojadę do Rynku?

rynku.tags: proper noun · masculine inanimate · genitive singular
rynku.why: Do takes the genitive. The e of Rynek is a fleeting vowel: Rynek, Rynku. In Kraków, Rynek on its own means Rynek Główny, the Main Square.
rynku.history: From Middle High German rinc, “ring, circle.”

idzie.tags: verb · imperfective · determinate · present · 3rd person singular
parts: root id- (d → dź before e, spelled dzi)
idzie.why: Iść is the determinate verb of walking: one trip, in one direction, under way now. Ania is on her way at this moment, so idzie. For walking around or habitually, Polish uses chodzić (line 5).

zla.why: W złą stronę, “in the wrong direction”: w + accusative for direction of movement, and the adjective agrees with strona.

strone.why: W + accusative expresses direction: w stronę Rynku, “towards the square.” Location uses the locative: po lewej stronie, “on the left side.”

zawrocic.why: Proszę + infinitive is the polite way to give instructions. Zawrócić means “to turn round and head back”; wrócić alone is “to return.”

parts: root of iść; i → j after a prefix
przejsc.why: Prze- means across or through, and usually comes with przez + accusative: przejść przez ulicę, przez most, przez park.

swiatlach.why: Światło means “light”; its plural, światła, is the everyday word for traffic lights. Na + locative for location: na światłach, “at the lights.”

pojade.tags: verb · perfective · non-past (future meaning) · 1st person singular
pojade.why: Jechać is for going by vehicle; iść is only on foot. Po- makes it perfective and adds the sense of setting off: pojadę, “I’ll go (by tram).”

tramwajem.why: The vehicle you travel by goes in the instrumental, with no preposition: jechać tramwajem, autobusem, pociągiem.

warto.why: Warto is impersonal: (nie) warto, or warto + infinitive, “it’s (not) worth doing.” It has no subject and doesn’t change; the past is warto było.

pieszo.why: Pieszo, “on foot,” shares its root with pieszy, “pedestrian.” In everyday speech you’ll also hear na piechotę.

dojdzie.tags: verb · perfective · non-past (future meaning) · 3rd person singular
parts: root of iść (d → dź, spelled dzi)
dojdzie.why: The same verb as Ania’s dojdę, now third person to agree with pani. A perfective present refers to the future: “you’ll get to Wawel.”

wawelu.tags: proper noun · masculine inanimate · genitive singular
wawelu.why: Do + genitive. Many masculine inanimate nouns take -u in the genitive: do Wawelu, do Rynku.
wawelu.history: Wawel is the hill above the Vistula with Kraków’s royal castle and cathedral.

skreci.tags: verb · perfective · non-past (future meaning) · 3rd person singular
skreci.why: Skręcić w + accusative means to turn into a street: skręcić w Grodzką, skręcić w lewo. Perfective, so the present form describes the next step.

grodzka.tags: adjective used as a street name · feminine · accusative singular
grodzka.why: Many street names are adjectives agreeing with an understood ulica, which is feminine: ulica Grodzka. After skręcić w it’s accusative, because w here means “into.”
grodzka.history: From gród, an old word for a fortified settlement.

pojdzie.tags: verb · perfective · non-past (future meaning) · 3rd person singular
parts: prefix po-, spelled pó in this verb
root of iść (d → dź, spelled dzi)
pojdzie.why: Pójść is the perfective of iść: “to set off, go.” Here it’s the next step of the route, so the present form refers to the future.

chodze.tags: verb · imperfective · indeterminate · present · 1st person singular
chodze.why: Chodzić is the indeterminate partner of iść: walking around, back and forth, or habitually. Codziennie chodzę, “every day I walk around.” Idę would mean she’s on her way somewhere right now.
chodze.compare: By vehicle: jeżdżę (jeździć), the indeterminate partner of jechać.

miescie.why: Po + locative means “around, all over”: po mieście, po parku. The stem changes before the locative -e: miasto → mieście.

mapa.why: Z meaning “with” takes the instrumental: z mapą.

parts: loc. sg. -e (the i marks n softened to ń)
telefonie.why: W + locative. The same softening as kino → kinie.

gubie.why: Imperfective because it keeps happening. Compare zgubiłam się in line 1: a single, completed event.

mieszkam.why: Polish uses the present tense for a situation that began in the past and still continues: mieszkam tu od dwudziestu lat, “I’ve lived here for twenty years.” English needs the perfect.

krakowie.tags: proper noun · masculine inanimate · locative singular
parts: loc. sg. -e (the i marks w softened)
krakowie.why: W + locative. The ó of Kraków becomes o when an ending follows: Krakowa, w Krakowie.

dwudziestu.why: Od takes the genitive, so the numeral is genitive too: od dwudziestu lat.

lat.why: Rok takes its plural from another word: dwa lata, pięć lat, od dwudziestu lat. The forms come from lato, “summer.”

wjechalem.tags: verb · perfective · past · 1st person singular · masculine
wjechalem.why: W- means “into,” with w + accusative: wjechać w ślepą uliczkę. The masculine has no agreement ending, and an e is inserted before the person marker.

you.m: You would say: wjechałem, as he does.

slepa.why: Ślepa uliczka, literally “a blind little street,” is a dead end. The adjective agrees with uliczka.

uliczke.why: A diminutive of ulica: c changes to cz before the suffix -k(a). Accusative because w here means “into.”

pocieszyl.tags: verb · perfective · past · 3rd person singular · masculine
pocieszyl.why: Masculine with no agreement ending, because it agrees with pan. Ania says it with irony: “well, that’s a comfort!”
pocieszyl.compare: To a woman: pocieszyła mnie pani.

exercises.prompt: Say about yourself: “I drove out of the garage” (wy- + jechać). ___ z garażu.

explain.m: Wy- means “out of”: wy + jecha + ł + e + m.
explain.f: Wy- means “out of”: wy + jecha + ł + a + m.

exercises.hint: W- means “into.” Which prefix means “out of”? Then check the learner setting at the top.

exercises.prompt: Ask: “How do I get to the station (on foot)?” Jak ___ do dworca?
exercises.explain: Do- means reaching a goal: do + jd + ę. After a prefix, the root id- of iść appears as jd-.
exercises.hint: Look at Ania’s question in the first line.

exercises.prompt: Tell someone politely to cross the bridge: Proszę ___ przez most.
exercises.explain: Prze- means “across” and goes with przez + accusative: prze + jś + ć.
exercises.hint: Look at przejść przez ulicę in line 2.

exercises.prompt: “I go to the gym every week”: Co tydzień ___ na siłownię.
exercises.explain: A regular, repeated trip takes the indeterminate chodzić: chodz + ę. Idę would mean you’re on your way right now.
exercises.hint: Compare codziennie chodzę with idzie pani.

exercises.explain: The vehicle you travel by is instrumental, with no preposition: tramwajem, autobusem, pociągiem.
